newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's 1996 inflation totals 10.03 pct - Fipe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's 1996 inflation totals 10.03 pct - Fipe.

text.p: Brazil's December inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) fell to 0.17 percent from 0.34 percent in November, taking 1996 yearly inflation to 10.03 percent, a Fipe official said.
Juarez Rizzieri, president of the Fipe institute, said 1996 Fipe inflation was the lowest annual rate since 1950.
Rizzieri also said he expected inflation to be even lower in 1997, between 6.0 percent and 7.0 percent.
Food and clothing prices were the main items contributing to lower inflation last year, he said. Food prices rose only 2.12 percent in 1996 and clothing prices fell 3.14 percent.
Items that lifted the index included a 28-percent rise in public rates, a 32-percent jump in rent costs and a 34-percent gain in school payments.
The president of the Fipe also announced the following breakdown of its weighted inflation index for December:
- Food -1.41 pct drop in the period
- Housing 0.44 pct rise in the period
- Transportation 2.40 pct rise in the period
- Personal expenses 0.50 pct rise in the period
- Clothing 0.33 pct rise in the period
- Health care 1.40 pct rise in the period
- Education 0.75 pct rise in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
